problems.stem: On a diagnosis table, a designer logs that a lesson on balancing chemical equations is hard 'because the steps interact and cannot be understood one at a time.' Which load category does this describe?
options: Extraneous load caused by poor layout.
Intrinsic load from high element interactivity in the task itself.
Germane load from the learner building a schema.
Extraneous load from a distracting background image.
problems.explanation: Intrinsic load comes from the inherent element interactivity of the material. When elements must be processed together to be understood, intrinsic load is high regardless of the layout.

problems.stem: Two diagnosis-table rows describe the same lesson. Row A: 'cluttered slide with unrelated clip art.' Row B: 'learner self-explains why each step follows.' Which row is extraneous load and which is germane load?
options: Row A is extraneous load to reduce; Row B is germane load to support.
Row A is germane load; Row B is extraneous load.
Both are intrinsic load and cannot be changed.
problems.explanation: Extraneous load is processing wasted on poor design (clip art) and should be cut. Germane load is processing devoted to building schemas (self-explanation) and should be supported.

problems.stem: An AI tutor reviewing your interaction-effects tutorial offers four edits. Which one should you REJECT because it manages load by deleting the concept rather than managing its load?
options: Move the line labels onto the plot and drop the rainbow legend.
Add pre-training on reading a single main effect before the interaction plot appears.
Simplify by removing the second factor so learners only track one variable.
Keep the predict-the-cell prompt even though it feels effortful.
problems.explanation: Removing the second factor deletes the very concept being taught: an interaction just is two factors and their joint effect. Intrinsic load is managed by sequencing (pre-training), extraneous load by cutting the legend, and germane effort (the prediction prompt) is protected. The bounded AI move is to accept the load-management edits and document the rejection with this reason.

problems.stem: A designer wants to lower intrinsic load on a genuinely complex procedure without dumbing it down. Which move is best justified by cognitive load theory?
options: Delete half the steps so the procedure is shorter.
Use sequencing and pre-training: teach the component concepts first, then present the whole procedure, so fewer novel elements interact at once.
Add decorative animation to make the procedure feel easier.
Present every step simultaneously so the learner sees the whole picture at once.
problems.explanation: Pre-training and segmenting manage intrinsic load by building partial schemas first, reducing the number of novel interacting elements processed at once, without removing essential content.
